name: Thudam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 bibliography (local hh/sources.bib) entries tagging Thudam: van Driem 2001 Languages of the Himalayas (overview; 'Thudam = Walungge [ola]'); von Fuerer-Haimendorf 1975 Himalayan Traders (ethnographic; 'Thudam = Walungge [ola], Naaba, Lhomi'); ISO CR 2019-038.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic check only: no grammar, phonology, sketch or wordlist record exists for Thudam in Glottolog 5.1 (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); the languoid page thud1238 (read online) is a retired/bookkeeping entry citing only the ISO change request.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page thud1238; Wikipedia 'Thudam language' (redirects to 'Central Tibetan'); Wikipedia 'Walung people' (accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Stubs; no phonology; only Clark 2019 and Tournadre 2014 cited for the language.

sources.citation: Clark, Micah. 2025. A Sociolinguistic Study of Walungge and Related Varieties Dhokpya and Thudam. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2025-003. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Republication of the 2019 report; only worth checking for an added phonological note or revised appendices. sil.org is could not be reached by automated download from here and the Internet Archive has no capture.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages: an introduction to the family of languages derived from Old Tibetan. Villejuif: LACITO Publications.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Thudam appears only in location/speaker-number passages: pp. 576-577 'The Lhomi and Thudam dialects.. are spoken in Sankhuwasabha district.. Thudam is spoken on a slope on a tributary of the Arun river'; p. 578 'Thudam: 1,800 (2000 census)'; Appendix 3 classification table puts Thudam in the Lhomi group (68.2, map H7), separate from the Gola group (69: Tokpe-Gola, Walungchung-Gola). Sec. 7.3.3 'Stress' (pp. 241-242) is family-level; nothing on Thudam stress.

sources.citation: Clark, Micah (written by); researched by Micah Clark, Janel Swenson & Sarah Shackelford. 2019. A Sociolinguistic Study of Walungge and Related Varieties Dhokpya and Thudam. Kathmandu: Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University & SIL International. 89 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 80650; republished as Journal of Language Survey Report 2025-003)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey only (ethnolinguistic identity, dialect mapping, lexical similarity 75-85% among Walung/Ghunsa/Lungthung/Thudam/Simbuk, perceived intelligibility, vitality). No phonology section; no mention of stress, tone or accent. p. 19: 'In terms of detailed linguistic documentation of Walungge, there are only two sources' (Bartram 2011; Caplow 2007). Thudam differs enough that only Thudam respondents showed noticeable difficulty understanding Walungge (abstract; p. 60).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request 2019-038 (submitted by Micah A. Clark, SIL Nepal; adopted 2020-03-19): merge [thw] Thudam into [ola] Walungge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; lexical similarity 75-85% and intelligibility figures; note that 'the term Walungge is not recognized by the people in Thudam as representing their language'.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas. 2014. The Tibetic languages and their classification. In Owen-Smith & Hill (eds.), Trans-Himalayan Linguistics, 105-129. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (author's preprint, 24 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists Walung and Tokpe Gola among SW-section languages; Thudam not mentioned; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bartram, Cathryn Virginia. 2011. An investigation of tone in Walungge. PhD thesis, School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London. 375 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Acoustic stress study of WALUNGGE (Taplejung villages Lungthung, Olangchung Gola, Yangma, Gunsa, Kyabla; four wordlist speakers 'living within the Walungge language area', pp. 112-113): sec. 5.2.6 p. 209 'as a general pattern Walungge has second syllable stress for words which are not verbs. Verbs have stress on their root, which is in general the first syllable'; minority of nouns with first-syllable stress (p. 211). Thudam appears only sociolinguistically: pp. 27-28 people from Thudam, Tokpe Gola and Olangchung Gola 'can communicate with each other with ease'; p. 31 Fuerer-Haimendorf's Thud…

sources.citation: Clark, Micah et al. 2017-2019. SIL Nepal / LinSuN survey field recordings: 325-item wordlist audio for Thudam village (basis of Clark 2019 Appendix C) and Recorded Story Playing text from a Thudam speaker.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only Thudam speech recordings known; an acoustic look at disyllables would be the first stress evidence for the Thudam variety itself (SIL Nepal archive; not published).

sources.citation: Bartram, Cathryn Virginia. 2010. Personal communication: notes regarding Dhokpya, Walungge, and Thudam; and 2017. Personal communication: interview regarding Walungge, Dhokpya, and Thudam (both cited in Clark 2019, References p. 88).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Bartram is the only phonologist who has worked on this language cluster and is on record as having notes on Thudam specifically; if any Thudam prosodic observations exist they are here (unpublished).

sources.citation: Caplow, Nancy J. 2009. The role of stress in Tibetan tonogenesis: a study in historical comparative acoustics. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 607 pp. (ProQuest 3350332 / docview 304850536).

sources.note: Glottolog/hh tag it for Tokpe Gola = Walungge [ola], the ISO language Thudam now belongs to; may contain acoustic stress data for the Gola-group variety closest to Thudam. Not open anywhere (see walu1241 record).

sources.citation: Vesalainen, Olavi & Marja Vesalainen. 1976. Lhomi phonemic summary. (Phonemic Summaries 12.) Kathmandu: SIL / Tribhuvan University; and Vesalainen, Olavi. 2016. A grammar sketch of Lhomi. Kathmandu/Dallas: SIL.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Tournadre & Suzuki 2023 place Thudam in the Lhomi group (68.2), not the Gola group; the Lhomi phonemic summary is the only published phonology of that group and would show whether the Lhomi-side stress pattern differs from Bartram's Walungge result. Describes Lhomi [lhm], not Thudam.
